title: Fly to Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: This is Nanga Parbat, in Gilgit-Baltistan, the ninth-highest mountain in the world.
Our journey starts at Raikot Bridge, on the Karakoram Highway, beside the Indus River.
From here, jeeps climb a narrow mountain track, about fifteen kilometres long, to the village of Tato.
Then comes a hike of two to three hours on foot, up through the forest.
And then the valley opens up: Fairy Meadows, at about three thousand three hundred metres.
The story goes that in nineteen fifty-three, the climber Hermann Buhl called it Märchenwiese, the fairy-tale meadow.
Today, visitors stay in wooden cottages and camps among the pine trees, with the mountain right in front of them.
From here, the trail continues towards Nanga Parbat's base camp, at almost four thousand metres.
And there it is: Nanga Parbat, eight thousand one hundred and twenty-six metres high.
It is known as the Killer Mountain, because so many climbers lost their lives on its slopes.
Hermann Buhl first reached its summit in nineteen fifty-three, and from Fairy Meadows, its great north face fills the sky.
